approach: Make `Athena::retry` accept a Closed(Stale) job. In `dispatch` (run/mod.rs) a new `stale_retry` step runs when no other seed applies. It reads the stale job's kept candidate and base from its records and merges the candidate onto the current tip once, before any producer call, with `land::merge_kept_candidate`. That function is backed by a new `Git::merge_tree_report` (`merge-tree --write-tree --name-only -z`), which keeps a conflicted tree and its unquoted paths. The step applies only when the stale job's `dispatch_branch` equals the checked-out branch and both commits still exist; otherwise the retry is the ordinary producer retry from the base. Clean merge: reuse `resume_candidate` with no planner and no producer. It re-merges against the prediction commit, builds the candidate from the merged tree, recomputes the change list and fingerprint, then runs admission, `check_and_verify` (checks, replay, verifier) and the unchanged `plan()` landing. A merge that adds nothing to the tip closes the job failed with a reason and no producer run. Conflict: the conflicted tree is committed as a seed and a producer retry starts from it through the existing `TreeRetrySeed` / `BaseThenTree` path; a gate between `producer_loop` and `candidate_stage` closes the job failed, before any check or verifier, if a conflicted path is unchanged from the seed or still holds marker lines. `plan()` and its fingerprint-equality bail are untouched. This revision, per the findings: the drain.rs test is dropped (drain.rs is not touched at all); README edits are kept and justified (three lines say a stale job is refused); the reader brief's wrong 'which was rejected' wording for a stale retry is left in briefs.rs, named in risks and D157, pinned by a reading.rs test of what the reader is told, and raised as a user question; D10's tradeoff line 293 gets a same-line note; the conflict test's first producer call is scripted to edit src/lib.rs line 1 and the test asserts the markers reached the producer.

decisions.choice: Decide clean-vs-conflict at dispatch time on `head`, before the dispatch commit, in `land::merge_kept_candidate(git, old_base, tip, old_candidate)`. `resume_candidate` redoes the merge against the prediction commit P to build the tree.
decisions.reason: The seed choice (resume vs seeded producer) fixes the brief that goes into the prediction commit, so it must come first. P differs from `head` only under records/, and an admitted candidate changes nothing there, so the second merge cannot newly conflict; if it does, the job closes failed with a reason and nothing lands unverified.

rejected.option: Decide inside `Athena::retry` at reading time
rejected.why: The tip can move between `retry` and `go`; `go` must decide on the tip it dispatches on. `retry` only needs to accept the job.

rejected.option: Re-apply the old candidate's diff onto the new base, as `resume_candidate` does today
rejected.why: That overwrites the other job's changes to the same files. Only a three-way merge keeps both.

decisions.choice: Add `Git::merge_tree_report(base, ours, theirs) -> MergeReport { tree, conflicts }` using `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only -z --merge-base=<base>`. Split stdout on NUL: first field is the tree (trim a newline), following non-empty fields are conflicted paths, the first empty field ends them. Exit 1 still returns the tree and paths; any other exit is an error. `merge_tree` (athena-git lib.rs:663) is unchanged.
decisions.reason: Without `-z` git C-quotes paths with spaces, quotes or non-ASCII characters, so the gate's `snapshot.dir().join(path)` and `show_file(seed, path)` would look up a different path. `merge_tree` returns None on a conflict and drops the tree; the producer seed needs the tree and paths. Needs git 2.38+; D19 pins 2.40 and the unit test uses the exact flags.

rejected.option: Parse newline output of `--name-only` without `-z`
rejected.why: Quoted paths for unusual file names break the gate.

rejected.option: Seed from the old candidate commit as `tree_seed` does for a rejected job
rejected.why: `BaseThenTree` would restore that commit's whole tree and undo the other job's landing; `tree_seed` refuses exactly that case (mod.rs 477-480).

rejected.option: On a conflict, plain retry from the new base with no seed
rejected.why: The request says to run the producer from the kept candidate; dropping it repeats the whole producer run.

decisions.choice: Build the clean path's `ResumeMark` from the stale job's committed Candidate and Verification records (stage Checks, empty check_runs). `report_gaps` and `left_criteria` stay empty and D157 says so.
decisions.reason: They exist only in `ResumeMark` (state.rs:491-493) and `Built` (producer.rs:31-35), feeding verification.rs:100-123 as notes to the verifier. No committed record holds them, and `settle_resume_marks` removes a closed job's mark. The stale job's verification already weighed them; the merged tree is checked and verified afresh.

rejected.option: Keep the resume mark when a job goes stale
rejected.why: Changes close-time bookkeeping for every job, and the mark describes the old tree.

rejected.option: Add a new record to carry the gaps
rejected.why: A schema change for a note the verifier already weighed; outside the listed files.

decisions.choice: Keep the conflict gate between `producer_loop` and `candidate_stage` (run/mod.rs ~1497). `RunContext` gains `seeded_conflicts: Vec<String>` (empty for every other job). `unresolved_conflicts(ctx, &snapshot)` flags a path whose bytes in `snapshot.dir()` equal `git.show_file(seed_commit, path)` (missing on both sides counts as unchanged) or that `land::has_conflict_markers` flags. A flagged path calls `self.failure(ctx, reason)` naming the paths, with no checks and no verifier.
decisions.reason: The seed commit and snapshot are both known there; candidate.rs (governed by D08) stays untouched. Markers in non-compiled files pass the checks, and modify/delete or rename conflicts leave no markers, so a per-path 'the producer touched this and removed the markers' rule is the sound one. A failed conflict retry loses the kept candidate on a later `athena retry` of that failed job (it matches neither `qualifies_for_tree_retry` nor `resumable_job`); D157 and the risks say so.

rejected.option: Fold the unresolved paths into the producer's one send-back (producer.rs 262-341)
rejected.why: Better for the user but widens the change to an unlisted file; raised as a user question.

rejected.option: Rely on the checks to reject marker-filled trees
rejected.why: They miss Markdown, TOML and data files, and modify/delete conflicts with no markers.

rejected.option: Edit candidate.rs 134-150
rejected.why: Governed by D08; would need a D156 reconciliation.

rejected.option: Let a producer keep a seeded version of a conflicted path unchanged
rejected.why: The rule cannot tell that from an unresolved conflict; such a retry fails with a reason naming the path. The cost is a failed retry, not a wrong landing.

decisions.choice: `stale_retry` applies only when the stale job's `dispatch_branch` (records.rs:633; recorded at mod.rs:1031) is non-empty and equals `self.git.current_branch()`, and `rev_parse` finds both the candidate and base commits. No ancestry condition. Otherwise it returns None and the retry is the ordinary producer retry from the base.
decisions.reason: `merge-tree --merge-base=<old_base>` applies the candidate's change onto any head, so ancestry is not needed for a correct merge; `plan()` still requires the new base to be an ancestor at landing. The branch condition stays: a job can be stale because another branch was checked out (close.rs 273-289, Plan::OtherBranch), and landing its candidate onto that branch with no producer run is a different act. A missing commit cannot be merged.

rejected.option: Keep the ancestry gate
rejected.why: No concrete reason; it sends one of the two stale causes back to a full producer run.

rejected.option: Merge onto whatever branch is checked out
rejected.why: Lands a candidate on a branch it was never dispatched on, unverified in that context.

decisions.choice: When the merge of the kept candidate onto P gives P's own tree, `resume_candidate` closes the retry job failed, with no producer run, with the reason 'the kept candidate's content is already on the branch tip (job <stale>)'.
decisions.reason: A plain retry would repeat the whole producer run for work that already landed, the cost this change exists to avoid.

rejected.option: Return None from `stale_retry` and run a producer retry from the base
rejected.why: Repeats the producer run for work already on the tip.

decisions.choice: Reuse `TreeRetrySeed` and the producer brief's existing fields for the conflict retry: `unmet` and `findings` empty, one redacted `must_address` line naming the stale job and the conflicted paths. briefs.rs is not touched.

risks.risk: The merge at `head` is clean but the merge against the prediction commit P (head plus dispatch records) conflicts.
risks.mitigation: `resume_candidate` redoes the three-way merge against P. On a conflict it calls `self.failure(ctx, ...)` and returns, so the job closes failed and nothing lands. An admitted candidate changes nothing under records/, so P's records-only difference cannot conflict.

risks.risk: A clean merge whose result equals the tip (the other job landed the same change) gives an empty candidate.
risks.mitigation: `resume_candidate` compares the merged tree with `tree_of(P)` and closes the job failed with 'the kept candidate's content is already on the branch tip (job X)', with no producer run. The `..._already_on_the_tip_...` lifecycle test covers it.

risks.risk: The kept candidate or base commit was garbage collected, or the stale job's dispatch branch is not the checked-out branch.
risks.mitigation: `stale_retry` returns None when `rev_parse` cannot find either commit or the branch differs; the job then runs an ordinary retry from the base, no worse than today. The other-branch lifecycle test covers the branch case. There is no ancestry gate: the three-way merge uses the recorded base explicitly, and `plan()` still requires the new base to be an ancestor at landing.

risks.risk: A producer leaves a conflict unresolved: markers in a non-compiled file, or a modify/delete or rename conflict with no markers.
risks.mitigation: The gate before `candidate_stage` closes the job failed, naming the paths, if any conflicted path is unchanged from the seed or still holds marker lines. No check or verifier runs on it. The unresolved-conflict lifecycle test covers it.

risks.risk: The gate fails a retry where the producer correctly keeps a conflicted path as seeded (for example keeps the modified side of a modify/delete conflict).
risks.mitigation: A deliberate cost, not a wrong landing; the reason names the path and D157 records the rule.

risks.risk: A failed conflict retry loses both the kept candidate and the producer's work: the failed job has no Candidate record and a later `athena retry` on it starts from the base.
risks.mitigation: Stated in D157. The user can run `athena retry` on the original stale job again, which merges the candidate afresh. Folding the paths into the producer's send-back needs producer.rs and is a user question.

risks.risk: Parallel jobs in this repository usually both add a bullet at the top of CHANGELOG.md or docs/decisions.md (plan.rs:461 lists them as shared append-only files), so the usual stale retry takes the conflict path and a producer run, not the no-producer path.
risks.mitigation: Stated in D157 and the CHANGELOG so users are not surprised. The conflict path still seeds the producer from the conflicted tree. A union merge for append-only files is a separate request.

risks.risk: The clean-merge verifier does not receive the original producer's `report_gaps` and `left_criteria`.
risks.mitigation: They are held only in the resume mark, which a closed job no longer has; the stale job's verification already passed with them, and the merged tree is checked and verified afresh. D157 states this.

risks.risk: The reader brief tells the reader a stale job 'was rejected', that its changes were discarded and that a retry starts from the base, which is false for a stale retry (it passed verification and its candidate is kept). The reader writes the reading the merged candidate is verified against.
risks.mitigation: The reader still receives the job's request, final reading, criteria, deliverables and corrections, and `end_state` stale in the prior-jobs section. The misstatement is named in D157, pinned by the reading.rs test, and raised as a user question; briefs.rs is not edited because it is prompt text outside the listed files.

risks.risk: Someone later adds Stale to the drain's retry set and the drain retries stale jobs automatically; this plan adds no test for the guard.
risks.mitigation: drain.rs:1654 stays unchanged; D157 states that automatic re-verification stays out. A guard test is offered as a user question.

risks.risk: Editing docs/decisions.md breaks the backtest's line-number links or the ontology test.
risks.mitigation: Keep lines 293 and 297 single lines, append D157 only at the end, avoid the three parsed phrases. The backtest test is in the verification run; reword a term if the ontology test objects.

risks.risk: The git flags are unsupported on an older git.
risks.mitigation: `merge-tree --write-tree --name-only -z` needs git 2.38 or later and D19 pins 2.40. The athena-git unit test exercises the exact flags, so an older git fails the test.

risks.risk: A user reads 'no producer run' as 'no model cost'.
risks.mitigation: `retry` goes through `ask`, so the reader still runs once; the CHANGELOG and tests say 'no producer run'.
